sections.title: Equivariant extension of $I_N$-finite tempered distributions on real flag varieties
sections.abstract: For a real reductive group and parabolic subgroups, the paper proves that certain equivariant tempered distributions defined on a stable open subset of a flag variety extend to the whole flag variety.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim that restriction from the whole flag variety onto any Q-stable Nash open subset is surjective on I_N-finite tempered distributions for each Casselman–Wallach representation of the Levi; the associated functor is also contravariantly exact.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: G is a real linear reductive group; P and Q are parabolic, the inducing representation is Casselman–Wallach, and the open set is Q-stable and Nash.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem concerns existence of extensions in this setting; it does not assert uniqueness or quantitative bounds.

sections.title: Planar cut-and-project sets with interval windows are bi-Lipschitz equivalent to lattices
sections.abstract: The paper proves lattice equivalence for planar cut-and-project sets in R^3 when the window is a segment or a finite union of intervals, without a Diophantine condition on the plane.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim every cut-and-project set in a non-rational plane in R^3 with a transverse segment window is bi-Lipschitz equivalent to Z^2, and extend the conclusion to finite unions of intervals.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The plane is not spanned by integer vectors, the segment is transverse to it, and the cut-and-project construction uses a translated integer lattice.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is window-dependent; the abstract contrasts interval windows with an earlier compact window of countable boundary that gives a non-lattice-equivalent set.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 1.886; Semantic Scholar listed 1 citation (current total; score component 1.386) and 2 cross-lists (component 0.500), the second-highest score.

sections.title: The weighted fundamental lemma for non-split groups
sections.abstract: The manuscript develops a Higgs-bundle and cohomological strategy to prove weighted fundamental-lemma identities for quasi-split unramified groups beyond the split case.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim the Weighted Fundamental Lemma for Lie algebras for general quasi-split unramified G and a parallel deduction of Waldspurger's nonstandard version; the introduction says these imply the Twisted Weighted Fundamental Lemma in good characteristic.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The work is formulated in equal characteristic for quasi-split unramified reductive groups; properness of the stated Higgs-bundle stack is given when the center is anisotropic, and the TWFL consequence is qualified by good characteristic.
sections.unique_caveat: This is an extensive 190-page preprint whose headline implications depend on characteristic and group hypotheses; those implications were not independently assessed here.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 1.636; Semantic Scholar listed 1 citation (current total; component 1.386) and 1 cross-list (component 0.250), third-highest in the pool.

sections.title: Non autonomous problems with nearly linear growth and Orlicz-Sobolev coefficients
sections.abstract: For non-autonomous variational integrals with nearly linear gradient growth, the authors establish local Lipschitz regularity of local minimizers under a balance involving ellipticity degeneration and Orlicz-Sobolev regularity of spatial coefficients.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim local Lipschitz regularity for local minimizers of integral functionals whose density has nearly linear growth, under the stated quantitative balance.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The domain is bounded and open in R^n, n≥2; the integrand depends on x and the gradient, with nearly linear growth in the gradient variable.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract does not state the exact balance condition or constants; the paper's theorem is needed before applying the result.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 1.386, driven by a Semantic Scholar total of 1 citation (score component 1.386); no cross-list component.

sections.title: On the interplay between the anisotropy and the regularity of the coefficients in non autonomous problems
sections.abstract: The authors prove local Lipschitz regularity for minimizers of non-autonomous variational integrals under a condition balancing coefficient regularity with non-uniform ellipticity.
sections.claimed_result: The abstract claims a sufficient condition for local Lipschitz regularity that extends and unifies earlier results, including the standard p-growth case.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A bounded open domain in R^n, n≥2, with a non-autonomous energy density satisfying general gradient-growth conditions; the condition couples x-regularity of the density and the ellipticity ratio.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract leaves the precise condition implicit; the theorem's hypotheses are essential and do not imply regularity for arbitrary coefficient roughness or ellipticity ratios.

sections.title: Nonlinear stability of periodic waves in the Benjamin-Ono equation
sections.abstract: Using conserved quantities and the integrable higher-order energy, the authors construct a Lyapunov functional and claim nonlinear orbital stability of periodic Benjamin–Ono waves under co-periodic and multiple-periodic perturbations.
sections.claimed_result: The abstract says positivity of the Lyapunov functional's second variation and coercivity for the stated periodic perturbations yield nonlinear orbital stability in the periodic domain.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The argument uses momentum, energy and integrability-based higher-order conservation, plus spectral information for the linearized operator.
sections.unique_caveat: The stated stability is for co-periodic and multiple-periodic perturbations in the periodic setting, not arbitrary perturbations or general non-integrable equations.

sections.title: Rigidity in the Lichnerowicz inequality for word-length semigroups
sections.abstract: The paper characterizes partial-cube Cayley graphs through equality cases in two noncommutative Lichnerowicz inequalities for word-length semigroups.
sections.claimed_result: For word-length semigroups on group von Neumann algebras, equality in either the complete Gamma2 criterion or the geometric Ricci criterion occurs exactly when the Cayley graph embeds isometrically into a hypercube.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The characterization concerns word-length semigroups on group von Neumann algebras and the specified noncommutative inequalities.
sections.unique_caveat: This is an equality-case characterization in the stated operator-algebraic setting, not a claim about arbitrary Cayley graphs or all spectral-gap inequalities.

sections.title: On the chromatic splitting conjecture in coheight 1
sections.abstract: The authors establish coheight-1 consequences predicted by the chromatic splitting conjecture using p-divisible groups, p-adic geometry, and a new two-tower isomorphism.
sections.claimed_result: The abstract claims a retract for the specified map of K(h−1)-local E-infinity rings when p−1 does not divide h−1, and an isomorphism when h=2 and p is odd; it also constructs a two-tower isomorphism for p-divisible groups in the stated setting.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Stable homotopy theory at chromatic height h, with the divisibility restriction on p and h for the retract; the stronger isomorphism statement is specified only for h=2 and odd p.
sections.unique_caveat: These consequences do not settle every prime-height case of the chromatic splitting conjecture; the stated divisibility and height hypotheses delimit the result.

sections.title: The regular N-gon maximizes first positive Neumann eigenvalue among simple polygons with at most N sides and fixed area
sections.abstract: For each N≥3, the authors claim the regular N-gon uniquely maximizes the area-scaled first positive Neumann eigenvalue among simple polygons of fixed area with at most N sides.
sections.claimed_result: The abstract says the regular polygon is the unique maximizer up to congruence, the optimum increases with N, and the result proves the polygonal Szegő–Weinberger conjecture; it also gives a triangular-lattice Voronoi-cell consequence.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Simple polygons with at most N sides and fixed area; the quantity is area times the first positive Neumann eigenvalue.
sections.unique_caveat: The extremal statement is restricted to polygons with a bounded side count and fixed area; it does not claim the analogous result for arbitrary planar domains.
